title: A or an? Listen to the first sound
description: Learn when to use a and an before singular countable nouns, with simple food and animal examples.

sections.heading: Use a before a consonant sound
paragraphs: Use a when the following word begins with a consonant sound. The article introduces one singular countable thing.

sections.heading: Use an before a vowel sound
paragraphs: Use an when the following word begins with a vowel sound. Listen to the sound rather than looking only at the first letter.
examples: an hour — the h is silent

sections.heading: The next word's sound matters
paragraphs: If an adjective comes before the noun, choose the article using the adjective's first sound. A word beginning with a vowel letter can still start with a consonant sound.
examples: a university — university starts with a /y/ sound
